children: The defence PSU’s radar systems will enhance aerial threat detection, with capabilities covering fighter-sized aircraft and smaller unmanned platforms

The Ministry of Defence has signed a Rs 770 crore contract with Bharat Electronics (BEL) for the supply of Improved Low Level Light Weight Radar (LLLR-I) systems to the Indian Army. The contract was signed in New Delhi on 21 October in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh, the ministry said.

The LLLR-I systems are designed to detect and track fighter-sized aircraft as well as mini and micro drones. The radars also have the capability to prioritise aerial targets, enabling the Army to identify potential threats and respond more effectively to unmanned aerial system (UAS) threats.

The ministry said the radar system will strengthen the Army’s ability to monitor low-level aerial threats, including smaller drones that can be difficult to detect. Its target-prioritisation capability is intended to support faster assessment of threats during aerial surveillance and operations.

The procurement is also part of the government’s efforts to increase indigenous defence manufacturing and strengthen the domestic defence ecosystem. According to the ministry, the contract aligns with the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision and is expected to support a resilient and globally competitive defence industry, including domestic MSMEs.

The latest contract adds to BEL’s series of defence orders secured during the year. In March, the ministry signed a contract worth around Rs 1,950 crore with BEL for two mountain radars and related equipment for the Indian Air Force, aimed at improving radar coverage in mountainous areas.

In May, BEL received a Rs 1,476 crore contract from the ministry for five ground-based mobile electronic systems for the Army. The deal required at least 72 per cent of the equipment’s content to be sourced domestically, supporting the government’s push for greater localisation in defence procurement.

BEL also announced a separate Rs 1,251 crore order in May for a ground-based mobile electronic intelligence system for the Army. Developed by the Defence Electronics Research Laboratory in Hyderabad and manufactured by BEL, the system can detect and locate radars and intercept and analyse communication signals.

On 13 October, BEL announced additional orders worth Rs 533 crore covering communication equipment, avionics, cybersecurity solutions, drones, jammers, software, upgrades, spare parts and services. BEL shares closed 1.59 per cent lower at Rs 371.20 on Wednesday.
